description: Sequencer built on Conway's Game of Life: a 32 by 20 wrapping board is stepped by a clock, and marked cells on it drive eight trigger outputs, with other Life-like rules available

params.text: Advances the simulation by one step
Returns the board to the seed, or randomises it if the menu says so
Randomises the board's current state without changing the seed
Sets how full a randomised board is, 0 to 1
Attenuates and inverts the RND % CV jack, -1 to 1, before that voltage is added to the density knob
Turns the automatic reset on and off
Sets how many steps run before the board resets itself, 1 to 64
Attenuates and inverts the LEN CV jack, -1 to 1, before that voltage is added to the length knob
Chooses what clicking the display does: Play ignores clicks, Edit seed draws the starting board, and the eight remaining positions each mark cells for one trigger set

inputs.text: A rise past 2V advances the simulation by one step
A rise past 2V returns the board to the seed, or randomises it if the menu says so
Divided by 10, scaled by its attenuverter and added to the density knob
A rise past 2V randomises the board's current state without changing the seed
A rise past 2V turns the automatic reset on and off; the menu can make it a plain gate instead, on while the voltage is high
Divided by 10, multiplied by 64 and by its attenuverter, then added to the length knob, the total clamped to 1 and 64

outputs.text: Its trigger set: a 10V pulse whenever any cell marked for that set becomes active, or a voltage from 0V to 10V for the share of that set's cells that are active, depending on the menu
A 10V pulse when the automatic reset length is reached

notes: the board is drawn on the display and edited by clicking it, which does nothing until the MODE knob is off Play; the display is not a control, so clicking it reaches no help line
the trigger sets work by marking cells as watch points; a set with no marked cells never puts anything out
every jack is monophonic, whatever is patched in
menu: Rule options — edits the birth and survival rule the simulation runs, with a list of the common Life-like rules to pick from
Trigger set options — per set: whether a marked cell counts while alive or only on the step it is born, whether its jack sends a trigger or a percentage, and a way to clear its marks
Randomize on manual reset — makes the reset button and jack randomise the board instead of returning it to the seed
Randomize on automatic reset — makes the automatic reset randomise the board instead of returning it to the seed
Momentary length enable input — makes the LEN TGL jack a plain gate rather than a toggle
